extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary/resignation proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards governing an affidavit of resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and the related disciplinary consequences, obligations, publications, and reinstatement presumptions for a registered patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit of resignation and exclude practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Acting USPTO Director has authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order invokes these statutory and regulatory provisions as the basis for approving the Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation and ordering exclusion on consent from practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must state consent is freely and voluntarily rendered (no coercion/duress)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent's affidavit must acknowledge that his consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and that he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the first explicit acknowledgment in the Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation; compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) requires such statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge awareness of pending disciplinary complaint and allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit must state the respondent is aware that a disciplinary complaint is pending and summarize the nature of the allegations (here: pattern and practice of neglecting thirty-three patent matters and nineteen trademark matters and allowing applications to become abandoned without clients' consent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the respondent's acknowledgment of the pending USPTO Disciplinary Proceeding No. D2012-32 and the specific allegations as a required element of the affidavit's disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge OED's opinion that respondent violated specified Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that the OED Director is of the opinion that the respondent violated particular Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists the specific disciplinary rules the OED Director alleges were violated and the affidavit must recognize OED's position (even if respondent does not admit actual violation).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglect of legal matters entrusted to the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes neglect of legal matters entrusted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged the respondent engaged in a pattern and practice of neglecting numerous patent and trademark matters entrusted to him and allowing applications to become abandoned without clients' consent; this citation ties that conduct to §10.77(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) & (b) via § 10.23(c)(8) — failing to inform client of important Office correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to inform a client of important Office correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites these provisions (via §10.23(c)(8)) as among the rules the OED Director believes were violated by not notifying clients about important USPTO communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the misconduct categories OED contends the respondent's actions fall within; invoked in combination with other §10.23 subdivisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged that aspects of the respondent's conduct fall within this proscription; cited specifically in the Order's recitation of alleged rule violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) & (b) via § 10.23(c)(2)(i) — knowingly giving false or misleading information to a client
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes knowingly giving false or misleading information to a client in connection with any immediate, prospective, or pending business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites this as one of the alleged violations (via the §10.23(c)(2)(i) cross-reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1) — failing to seek lawful objectives of a client
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED contends the respondent's neglect prejudiced clients by failing to pursue their lawful objectives; this rule is cited to characterize that failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(3) — prejudicing or damaging a client
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes prejudicing or damaging a client during the course of a professional relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites this provision to describe the consequences of the alleged neglect and abandonment of client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.89(c)(6) — intentional or habitual violations of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes intentional or habitual violations of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged that the respondent's pattern of conduct constituted intentional or habitual violations; this rule is cited to encompass repeated misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in any other conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as a catch-all for conduct that undermines professional fitness; included in the list of alleged violations tied to the respondent's conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge reinstatement presumptions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit must acknowledge that, if and when the respondent applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume for the limited purpose of determining the application that (i) the allegations in the disciplinary complaint are true and (ii) the respondent could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent in this case acknowledged this presumption in his affidavit even though he did not admit the alleged rule violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge understanding of relevant procedural regs and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must have fully read and understand 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 and be aware of the legal and factual consequences of requesting and consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit explicitly states the respondent's awareness of these provisions and the consequences of exclusion and possible reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO as part of an affidavit of resignation under § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order approves the affidavit and orders exclusion on consent effective the date of the Final Order; consent is an explicit element of the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and effective exclusion ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: When the affidavit complies with § 11.27(a), the Acting Director may approve the Affidavit of Resignation and order the respondent excluded on consent from practice effective on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation shall be, and hereby is, approved' and orders exclusion beginning on the date the Final Order is signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED Reading Room and Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs publication in both locations and provides the exact notice-language to be used in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion, allegations, and reinstatement presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (practitioner duties upon exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as required by the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Order does not restate §11.58's text, it mandates compliance by the respondent (typically duties such as providing notice to clients and closing out practice responsibilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 (OED duties upon acceptance of resignation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 as required by the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires the OED to follow the obligations set out in §11.59 when accepting an affidavit of resignation and ordering exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 when seeking reinstatement, including the consequences and presumptions applicable to prior accepted resignations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order emphasizes that the respondent's acknowledgments in the affidavit (including the presumptions about the truth of allegations) will govern the reinstatement review under §11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs — each party bears own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and the respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies that neither side will be awarded costs against the other for the proceedings and implementation of the agreement.
